summary: The main thread's stack, as mono's collector queries it: one MEM_PRIVATE reservation of SizeOfStackReserve from TEB.DeallocationStack, allocation protection read-write; reserved below StackLimit - 3 pages, those 3 pages committed with PAGE_GUARD, committed read-write from StackLimit to StackBase; VirtualQuery's BaseAddress is the queried page; GetCurrentThreadStackLimits answers DeallocationStack and StackBase; the last error is left.

evidence.quote: The system commits additional pages from the reserved stack memory as they are needed, until either the stack reaches the reserved size minus one page (which is used as a guard page to prevent stack overflow) or the system is so low on memory that the operation fails.

open_questions: Where the stack pointer's page lies above StackLimit depends on how far the runner's stack had grown (2 or 3 pages in runs 38114383995, 38114385651, 38114444717, 38114446614); the derive drops base_address from query.sp and query.base_minus_one, and query.limit and query.below_limit keep the layout.

w2m commits all but 4 pages of the 1 MB at the start and never moves StackLimit; Windows commits on demand through the guard pages. A program that reads StackLimit to size its stack sees more room in w2m.
The page speaks of one guard page; every run shows a 3-page PAGE_GUARD region below StackLimit (query.below_limit, query.below_guard). The rows are followed.
